title: 2026 U.S. House of Representatives Election in Pennsylvania's 16th Congressional District
description: The 2026 election for Pennsylvania's 16th Congressional District pits seven-term Republican incumbent Mike Kelly against Democratic challenger Justin Wagner. The district covers northwestern Pennsylvania, including Erie, Butler, and Mercer counties, and has a Cook Partisan Voting Index of R+11. Kelly, a senior member of the Ways and Means Committee, is seeking his ninth term after first being elected in 2010. Wagner, a U.S. Army veteran and automation engineer, is running on a platform focused on workers' rights and economic fairness in what is considered a safe Republican seat. The general election is scheduled for November 3, 2026.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race as of July 2026.

candidates.name: Mike Kelly
candidates.summary: Mike Kelly is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 16th Congressional District, first elected in 2010. He serves on the House Ways and Means Committee and chairs the Subcommittee on Tax, and previously led a bipartisan task force investigating assassination attempts against President Donald Trump. A former car dealership owner and member of the Butler Area School Board and Butler County Council, Kelly is known for his conservative voting record and focus on tax reform and economic issues.

candidates.name: Justin Wagner
candidates.summary: Justin Wagner is the Democratic nominee for Pennsylvania's 16th Congressional District. He is a U.S. Army veteran who served in Iraq, an automation engineer, and a life sciences professional from Mercer County. Wagner's campaign focuses on workers' rights, fair wages, and challenging corporate power, positioning himself as a pro-union, pro-worker alternative to the incumbent.

forecast.rationale: No public polling exists for this race, which tempers confidence. However, the available structural data strongly points to a safe Republican hold: the district carries a Cook PVI of R+11, seven-term incumbent Mike Kelly (first elected in 2010) holds seniority on the Ways and Means Committee, and the race description itself characterizes the seat as safe Republican. Democratic challenger Justin Wagner is a credible U.S. Army veteran and engineer, but the district's partisan lean and Kelly's entrenched incumbency provide no contrary signal. Without any polling evidence, the forecast relies on these fundamentals, which overwhelmingly favor the Republican incumbent.
